businessDescription: AI-powered corporate English training platform — 24/7 conversational AI practice, real-time HR analytics, and industry-specific modules that reduce training costs by 80% and accelerate fluency 40% faster than traditional classroom methods. 70,000+ active learners across global teams.
voice: Outcomes-first and data-backed — makes the business case for AI language training with specifics, then shows how real fluency (not just certification) changes what teams can actually do.
targetAudience: HR managers and L&D leaders at global companies whose teams work across languages — dealing with the real cost of language gaps in meetings, presentations, client calls, and cross-functional collaboration. They want measurable outcomes and easy rollout, not another course nobody finishes.

hardConstraints.rule: Always cite sources inline with hyperlinks.
Never make up statistics — only use numbers that appear in the research notes.
hardConstraints.example: If no stat is found, write 'data unavailable' rather than estimating.

hardConstraints.rule: Every post must have a clear thesis stated in the introduction.
hardConstraints.example: First paragraph ends with a specific, defensible claim the post will prove.

hardConstraints.rule: Never position language training as 'fixing' employees — frame it as removing a barrier to performance.
hardConstraints.example: The problem isn't the employee's intelligence or effort. It's that a language gap silences capable people.

softPreferences.preference: Lead with the business cost of the language gap — not the solution.
softPreferences.example: Open with: what actually goes wrong when teams can't communicate confidently in English? Lost deals, slower decisions, ideas that never get voiced.

softPreferences.preference: Use the measurement frame — 'you can't manage training you can't measure' is their own tagline.
softPreferences.example: Connect L&D investment to trackable outcomes: speaking time, fluency progression, usage frequency.

softPreferences.preference: Acknowledge that most corporate language training fails — then explain why TalkParty's model is different.
softPreferences.example: 10 minutes a day beats 1 hour a week that no one actually does. Micro-learning that fits into real work schedules.

softPreferences.preference: Keep paragraphs short — HR leaders scan content between meetings.
softPreferences.example: Under 5 sentences. Use data points as standalone pull moments, not buried in long paragraphs.

avoidTopics: content that implies non-native English speakers are less capable or intelligent
